Data dictionaries and model checks

Unit 2 · Week 2 · Lesson 4 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the entities and relationships chapter, relationships-workbook.md, relationships-answers.md, equipment-model.svg and the four model CSVs (Borrower, Category, Equipment, Loan). Use fictional data and a disposable copy or paper. No SQL setup or student account is required. Explained answers are public.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Data dictionaries and model checks

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Use the equipment desk scenario from Week 1. Document each field and test the design against examples. All activities are ungraded. Suggested timings can be adjusted. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

2. A diagram and a dictionary

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Recall and partner explanation

A data dictionary records field names, types, sizes, meanings and constraints. It complements the diagram. Include required/optional status, key roles, formats and defaults where relevant. The model uses conceptual types before mapping to a chosen DBMS. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

3. Loan identifiers in the dictionary

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example with teacher explanation

The dictionary gives maximum text lengths chosen for this exercise, not universal limits. BorrowerID follows B plus three digits and EquipmentID E plus two digits. Text preserves letters and leading zeros. Each FK refers to the matching identifier field in its parent table. The exact DBMS type and enforcement come later. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

4. Dates, return status and defaults

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Prediction and teacher modelling

Date and Boolean storage sizes depend on the DBMS. A displayed date format is not necessarily the storage format. The False default applies when a new loan omits a status value; it does not reset historical loans. CSV values are text encodings until converted. Choose integer for counts, float for approximate measured mass, text for labels, date for due date and Boolean for return status. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

5. Counterexamples for a design

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Paired practice with exchanged roles

Partners state allowed/refused and explain the specific rule. Duplicate L001 and nonexistent B999 are invalid. For this learning model, restrict deletion of B001 while loans refer to it until references are resolved deliberately. C04 with no equipment is allowed. Format checks alone cannot prove a stored fact is true. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

6. Dictionary and workbook practice

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application

Use workbook questions 10–12 and revisit question 7. Loan has LoanID, BorrowerID, EquipmentID, DueDate and Returned. Include type, maximum text size or DBMS-dependent size, meaning, key/reference, required status and relevant format/default. Identifiers are text. Default False applies to new loans. Ask for a justified deletion policy that keeps loan history. Support learners with the worked tables before a fresh independent example. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

7. A default is not a bulk update

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Misconception check with reasons

No. A default supplies a value for a new record when omitted in the appropriate operation. It does not rewrite existing records. Changing an existing record needs an explicit update, which must also meet the configured constraints. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

8. A new requirement changes the model

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Reflection and a fresh example

A single EquipmentID stores one item reference. Do not overwrite the field or store a comma-separated list while claiming the existing design is unchanged. Further modelling could separate the loan event from its item lines in a linking/detail table, with agreed item and return rules. Ask which facts belong to the whole event and which belong to each item. This is an extension discussion, not a silent change to the four-table dataset. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.
